items.prompt: A narrow invoice-classification prototype is ready for every finance team, but its evidence covers one queue and there is no production monitor, handoff owner, or rollback condition. What lifecycle plan is appropriate?
constraints: A controlled pilot, human fallback, monitoring, handoff, and feedback loop are feasible.
The prototype’s evidence is limited to one queue.
Expansion needs explicit phase exits and recovery ownership.

options.text: Define phase exits, pilot with monitoring and fallback, complete handoff, and iterate from production evidence before scaling.
Roll out all teams from the demo, add monitoring after the first incident, and use finance feedback to adjust coverage.
Keep the prototype isolated, refine its queue score, and revisit rollout when every finance document is known.
Scale one queue at a time on a green aggregate score, adding rollback ownership after expansion.

feedback.Reason: Prototype capability does not prove broad coverage or operability; staged phase exits, fallback, handoff, monitoring, and feedback create evidence for expansion.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends a living evaluation suite combined with production monitoring and feedback as systems evolve.
Details.scenarioApplication: Set discovery and design criteria, run a bounded queue pilot with a human fallback and monitor, assign handoff and rollback owners, and use production cases for iteration.
Details.errorCorrection: Immediate rollout lacks recovery and coverage evidence, indefinite isolation prevents learning, and aggregate scores do not replace phase ownership.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If all finance queues, monitoring, owners, and rollback had already been validated, broad rollout could be the next phase exit.
Details.transfer: Move through lifecycle gates with evidence, fallback, ownership, and production feedback before expanding scope.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: A broad rollout before monitoring and handoff ownership increases exposure while evidence still covers one queue.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Permanent isolation prevents the production feedback needed to validate and improve the lifecycle.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: An aggregate score and post-expansion rollback assignment do not establish slice coverage or recovery ownership.

items.prompt: After handoff, a new document type fails in production while no team owns evaluation updates or alerts; the original aggregate score remains green. What is the lifecycle diagnosis?
constraints: The new type is absent from the offline suite.
Ownership and cadence can still be assigned.

options.text: Raise the aggregate threshold and route the new document type to a review queue until its score stabilizes.
Replace the model immediately, then assign an alert owner if the new type continues failing after the change.
Assign evaluation and alert owners, inspect traces, add the new slice, and schedule an evidence-based iteration.
Return ownership to the prototype author, let that person revise the prompt, and compare complaints at the next review.

feedback.Reason: The gap is in post-handoff ownership and slice coverage; production evidence must enter a living evaluation before a model change is chosen.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends reading production transcripts and evolving the evaluation suite so it remains useful over time.
Details.scenarioApplication: Name alert and evaluation owners, review representative failures, add the new type to the suite, and schedule the model or prompt decision from its evidence.
Details.errorCorrection: Threshold changes and suppression hide the slice, an immediate model replacement confounds process and model causes, and one former author is not an ownership model.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the type were covered and an alert owner had triaged the trace, a model or prompt change could be evaluated next.
Details.transfer: When handoff exposes a new failure, repair ownership and evaluation coverage before changing the model.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A threshold and review queue may contain exposure, but they do not add the missing slice or durable owners.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Changing the model before diagnosing the handoff and coverage gap confounds the cause.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A prototype author cannot substitute for post-handoff operational and evaluation ownership.

items.prompt: A legal research assistant moves from discovery to a bounded pilot and later handoff; citation quality, escalation, latency, and post-handoff ownership are disputed. Select TWO lifecycle controls.
constraints: Phase exit criteria can be made explicit.
Named monitoring, feedback, evaluation, rollback, and iteration owners are available.

options.text: Treat code merge as handoff completion and let the implementation owner inherit every future decision.
Set evidence-based exit criteria for discovery, pilot, and handoff, including citation, escalation, and latency checks.
Use the original demo as the permanent quality baseline and review disputes when users complain.
Let one prototype owner decide readiness and retain an informal escalation chat.
Assign named owners for monitoring, feedback, evaluation maintenance, rollback, iteration, and review cadence after transfer.

feedback.Reason: Lifecycle transitions need evidence to exit each phase and explicit accountability after transfer; code merge or a demo does not prove citation or escalation readiness.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic defines evaluations through tasks, trials, graders, transcripts, outcomes, and a harness, supporting explicit evidence and ownership across lifecycle decisions.
Details.scenarioApplication: Set phase checks for citation, escalation, and tail latency, then name each post-handoff owner and cadence for alerts, suite updates, rollback, and iteration.
Details.errorCorrection: Merge, demos, complaint-driven review, and informal ownership leave the service contract and response duties unverified.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the system were a private prototype with no users, side effects, or handoff, phase ownership could remain with the prototype team.
Details.transfer: Make every lifecycle exit evidence-based and assign ownership for the decisions that continue after handoff.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Code merge does not prove user-facing citation or escalation behavior.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A static demo and complaints are weak evidence for ongoing lifecycle decisions.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: One informal owner cannot cover monitoring, evaluation maintenance, rollback, and transfer accountability.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.b: Exit criteria make the disputed behavior observable before phase transition.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: Named owners and cadence preserve accountability after the system changes hands.

items.prompt: A payroll assistant used an outdated tax table; after containment, the team finds no freshness check, data owner, human review boundary, or runbook path for future updates. What lifecycle change is needed?
constraints: Future data changes can be checked, monitored, evaluated, and rolled back under human review.
A trusted data owner can be assigned.

options.text: Close the incident after replacing the table, mention current taxes in the prompt, and rely on payroll reviewers to flag stale data.
Wait for another tax incident, then add a freshness check and assign an owner when volume justifies it.
Replace the model, preserve the current table-update process, and review stale-data complaints in the next release.
Add freshness checks and incident cases, document human review, assign a data owner, and update handoff, monitoring, and rollback.

feedback.Reason: Containment must become a recurring lifecycle control with freshness, ownership, review, and regression evidence rather than a one-off source replacement.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends treating evaluation as a living suite that incorporates production failures and supports iterative improvement.
Details.scenarioApplication: Check table freshness before use, alert the data owner, add the stale-table case to evaluation, require human review for uncertain updates, and document rollback.
Details.errorCorrection: Prompt wording and a source replacement do not monitor future data, waiting repeats the harm, and model capability is unrelated to table freshness.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a trusted pipeline already enforced freshness and alerted an owner, the post-incident change could focus on preserving the regression case and review boundary.
Details.transfer: Convert incidents into owned freshness, evaluation, handoff, and rollback controls that prevent recurrence.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Prompt context and reviewer vigilance do not establish source freshness, a data owner, or a repeatable update runbook.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Waiting repeats a known payroll risk and makes ownership contingent on another incident.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Model replacement does not repair stale-source controls or define human review and rollback.

items.prompt: A provider announces retirement of the model version used by a production assistant. Current quality is green, but the replacement changes cost, context behavior, and an approval-sensitive output schema. What should precede cutover?
constraints: The living suite can run production-shaped slices.
The handoff contract and owners can be updated.
Rollback and a post-cutover review are available.

options.text: Re-run quality, safety, schema, cost, and latency; update owners; canary the replacement with rollback and post-cutover review.
Switch immediately because current quality is green, then ask users to report context, cost, or schema regressions.
Extend the current version under an exception, waiting for a replacement with equivalent cost, context, and schema results.
Update the model ID, rely on existing approval, and use parser failures to decide whether a later rollback is needed.

feedback.Reason: Retirement is a lifecycle transition with changed behavior and operations, so evidence, updated ownership, canary exposure, rollback, and review must precede cutover.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends maintaining a living evaluation suite and combining it with production monitoring and feedback as systems evolve.
Details.scenarioApplication: Run production-shaped quality and safety cases, validate parser and approval contracts, compare cost and latency, update the handoff, canary the replacement, and retain rollback.
Details.errorCorrection: Green current quality says nothing about replacement compatibility, indefinite pinning blocks a required transition, and an approval step cannot validate all changed schemas.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the replacement were contract-compatible, fully covered by regression evidence, and rollback ownership already assigned, cutover could use a shorter validation gate.
Details.transfer: Treat model retirement as a versioned lifecycle change requiring contract evidence, controlled exposure, and owned recovery.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Green current quality says nothing about the replacement’s schema, context, cost, or latency before exposure.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: An exception may buy time, but waiting for equivalent behavior without a staged comparison risks the sunset and leaves owners unprepared.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Existing approval may not catch parser, context, cost, or latency regressions before users encounter them.

items.prompt: A pilot has passed its quality and safety gates, and a production-readiness review shows monitoring, fallback, rollback, escalation, and handoff controls are complete and exercised. Trained reviewers cover the current high-risk traffic, the review queue has capacity for measured demand, and the sponsor requests a controlled rollout. Select TWO: Which actions fit the completed readiness evidence?
constraints: The current traffic mix, reviewer training and coverage, queue-capacity measurements, monitoring, fallback, rollback, escalation, handoff owners, and passed phase gates are recorded and can be checked.

options.text: Advance the supported traffic into a controlled rollout with monitoring, trained reviewer coverage, fallback, rollback, and named owners.
Keep the pilot bounded until every possible future traffic segment and reviewer queue has been exercised.
Keep new traffic classes outside the rollout until their evidence and reviewer capacity pass explicit expansion gates.
Roll out broadly because the current gates are green and let reviewers discover capacity limits during exposure.
Advance the supported class but defer the explicit human-review checkpoint and expansion gates until the first post-rollout review.

feedback.Reason: Advance the supported traffic into a controlled rollout with active monitoring, trained reviewer coverage, fallback and rollback, named owners, and explicit expansion gates; keep new traffic classes outside the rollout until their evidence and capacity pass. The decisive constraint is All declared readiness controls are complete and exercised, and trained reviewer capacity fits the supported traffic; the lifecycle may advance through a controlled rollout with continued gates and recovery ownership.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends a living evaluation suite combined with production monitoring and feedback as systems evolve. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
Details.scenarioApplication: Advance the supported traffic into a controlled rollout with active monitoring, trained reviewer coverage, fallback and rollback, named owners, and explicit expansion gates; keep new traffic classes outside the rollout until their evidence and capacity pass.
Details.errorCorrection: It treats unplanned future scope as a prerequisite for a controlled release and delays the phase decision despite complete evidence for the supported class; expansion can remain gated. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If reviewer training, queue capacity, monitoring, fallback, rollback, or escalation evidence were missing or untested, retain the existing bounded-pilot hold until the readiness gate passes.
Details.transfer: Advance the evidenced scope with recovery ownership while keeping unproven traffic outside the current phase.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Unplanned future scope is not a prerequisite for a controlled release whose current class has complete evidence and capacity.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Broad rollout discards the supported-class boundary and can exceed trained reviewer capacity before monitoring reacts.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.e: Current readiness depends on the human-review checkpoint and expansion gates remaining active before exposure; postponing them discards controls that justified the rollout.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.a: Required control: Advance the supported traffic into a controlled rollout with monitoring, trained reviewer coverage, fallback, rollback, and named owners.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.c: Required control: Keep new traffic classes outside the rollout until their evidence and reviewer capacity pass explicit expansion gates.

items.prompt: The model and service remain technically valid, but the business process they support has been retired. After an inventory, the accountable owner confirms that no authorized consumers remain, and an organization-approved retention period for records is documented. Select TWO: Which actions complete the lifecycle exit?
constraints: The consumer inventory, owner confirmation, service and tool dependency map, residual-traffic check, decommission plan, and organization-approved retention period are recorded before shutdown.

options.text: Keep the service dormant and upgrade it on the normal lifecycle cadence in case the retired process returns.
Decommission the agent, its tools, and associated operational data under the organization-approved retention policy, and revoke active paths.
Delete all records immediately regardless of the approved retention period so no operational data remains.
Record owner sign-off and monitor for residual traffic until closure is confirmed.
Keep the tools and data available for a possible future consumer even though the inventory found none.

feedback.Reason: Decommission the agent, its tools, and associated operational data under the organization-approved retention policy, revoke active paths, record owner sign-off, and monitor for residual traffic until closure is confirmed. The decisive constraint is A retired business process with zero authorized consumers does not justify continued agent operation; decommission the agent, tools, and associated data according to the approved retention policy and verify closure.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends a living evaluation suite combined with production monitoring and feedback as systems evolve. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
Details.scenarioApplication: Decommission the agent, its tools, and associated operational data under the organization-approved retention policy, revoke active paths, record owner sign-off, and monitor for residual traffic until closure is confirmed.
Details.errorCorrection: The inventory and owner confirmation establish zero authorized consumers, so continued tools and data create avoidable operational surface; the approved retention and closure plan supplies the correct exit. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If an authorized consumer or active business process remained, retain a bounded service and apply the normal evaluation, monitoring, and phase gates instead of decommissioning it.
Details.transfer: Retire a service when its authorized business use ends, while preserving approved records and proving that active paths are closed.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Zero authorized consumers and a documented exit plan make continued tools and data avoidable operational surface.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Immediate deletion violates the approved retention policy and removes evidence needed for governed closure.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.e: Retaining an unowned service and its tools contradicts the owner-confirmed retirement and residual-traffic check.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.b: Required control: Decommission the agent, its tools, and associated operational data under the organization-approved retention policy, and revoke active paths.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.d: Required control: Record owner sign-off and monitor for residual traffic until closure is confirmed.
